state: Goal `core-str-2-3`: `Core\Str::graphemes`, `indexOf`, `isEmpty`, `join`, `lastIndexOf`, `lines`, `lower` and `lowerFirst` are complete (`bun nv proofs --id` says so for each). `lines` and `Core\IO::lines` now build their list through `crate::str::lines_array`, which counts the lines, asks `nvs_runtime::affordable` for the whole list and reserves it. Before that, a text of line breaks alone grew the list to many times the memory limit before the breach was reported. The `2/3` check still names `normalize`, `padEnd`, `padStart`, `repeat` and `replace` with no proofs. Gaps `nvs-stdlib/a-match-inside-a-character-reports-the-wrong-position` and `nvs-stdlib/case-conversion-builds-its-result-outside-the` (both M12) are open. Any change to the code of `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs` makes every `Core\Str` perf record stale. Re-measure them all in the same session with `bun nv proofs --record-perf --only …`, naming each `benches/members/core/Str/*.nvs` except `length.scale`. A change to a card or a test does not make a record stale.

next.title: feature proofs, one member per slice

items.text: **`Core\Str::normalize`** — owes about.md, three examples, an attack, a bench, a Rust `covers:` test and a card in plain words (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`); its card is `NORMALIZE_DOC`, near `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs:1416`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs:3487`
**`Core\Str::padStart`** — the same proofs. `crates/nvs-stdlib/tests/allocation_policy.rs:234` already calls it and may take the `covers:` marker. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs:3280`
**`Core\Str::padEnd`** — the same proofs, and the same Rust test file. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs:3296`

backlog: `Core\Str::replace` owes the same proofs, and after it the `3/3` check's members (`data/goals/core-str-2-3.json`).

Other members that append to an array in a loop over their input (`split`, `chunk`, `graphemes`, `codePoints`) may grow past the ceiling the way `lines` did. `lines_array` in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs` is the pattern. The runtime-wide fix is gap `nvs-stdlib/regex-split-builds-its-array-past-the` (M12).
